beats.intro: Chapter forty-one. [[sub]]A long list of numbers is hard to read at a glance. A good display lets you see the pattern.
beats.twoway: A two-way table sorts one group by two questions at once. [[q]]Thirty-six students took a test. Did they go to the review session, and did they pass? [[cols]]The columns split the students by the review. [[rows]]The rows split them by the result. [[cells]]Each cell counts the students who fit both. Eighteen did the review and passed. [[tot]]Adding across a row gives a row total. Adding down a column gives a column total. [[all]]Both ways, the totals add up to all thirty-six students. [[cmp]]Now compare. Of the twenty-one students who did the review, eighteen passed. [[cmp2]]Of the fifteen who skipped it, only six passed. [[rel]]The table suggests a relationship: students who did the review were more likely to pass.
beats.q1: Quick check. Click the right cell.
beats.lineplot: A line plot shows the frequency of each value, meaning how often it occurs. [[data]]Twelve students said how many pets they have. [[line]]Draw a number line that covers every answer, [[marks]]then put one x above the value for each answer. [[read]]Now the pattern is easy to see. [[mode]]One pet is the most common answer, so the mode is one. [[range]]The answers run from zero to four, so the range is four.
beats.histogram: A histogram also shows frequency, but for equal intervals instead of single values. [[data]]Here are twenty students' homework times, in minutes. [[bins]]Split the scale into intervals of ten minutes: zero to nine, ten to nineteen, and so on. [[fill]]Each time adds one to the height of its interval's bar. [[gap]]The bars touch, because the intervals cover the whole scale with no gaps. [[read]]The tallest bar shows the most common interval: twenty to twenty-nine minutes.
beats.boxplot: A box plot shows how a data set is spread out, using just five numbers. [[data]]Here are eleven values, in order, on a number line. [[med]]First find the median, the middle value. It's eleven, and it splits the data into a lower half and an upper half. [[q1]]The median of the lower half is the lower quartile, Q one. Here it's six. [[q3]]The median of the upper half is the upper quartile, Q three. Here it's fifteen. [[ends]]The minimum is two, and the maximum is twenty-four. [[box]]Draw a box from Q one to Q three, with a line at the median, [[wh]]then whiskers out to the minimum and the maximum.
beats.quarters: Those five numbers cut the data into four parts, [[four]]and each part holds about a quarter of the values. [[mid]]So the box holds the middle half of the data. [[long]]A long part means the values in it are spread out. [[short]]A short part means they're bunched close together. [[ex]]Here, the right whisker is the longest part: the largest values are the most spread out.
beats.q3: Quick check. Find the median and the quartiles.
beats.scatter: A scatter plot compares two sets of data that come in pairs. [[tab]]Ten students report the hours they studied and their test scores. [[pt]]Each student becomes an ordered pair: hours across, score up. [[all]]Plot every student. [[trend]]The points drift upward: more studying tends to go with a higher score. [[fit]]A line of best fit runs through the middle of the points to show that trend. It doesn't have to pass through any of them.
beats.corr: The trend in a scatter plot is called a correlation. [[pos]]Positive correlation: as one value goes up, the other tends to go up too. [[neg]]Negative correlation: as one value goes up, the other tends to go down, like a car's age and its price. [[none]]No correlation: the points show no trend, like shoe size and birthday month. [[tend]]Notice the word tends. A correlation describes the overall pattern, not every single point.
beats.q4: Quick check. Which plot shows a negative correlation?
beats.wrap: Each display answers a different question. [[w1]]A two-way table counts one group by two categories at once. [[w2]]Line plots and histograms show how often values occur. [[w3]]A box plot summarizes the spread with five numbers. [[w4]]A scatter plot shows whether two sets of data are related. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
